overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of the questions that come with regular AI use. You'll be asked about disclosure and who answers for AI-assisted work, AI-text detectors, what happens to information you give a tool, the arrangements a tool can come under, what to keep out of a prompt, copyright in AI outputs, and the evidence on AI, skill, and learning.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: Under the positions of COPE and the ICMJE, who answers for the content of a paper when an AI tool produced part of it?

options.html: The developer of the AI tool, for the parts it produced
options.text: The developer of the AI tool, for the parts it produced
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on disclosure rules in scholarly publishing.

options.html: The AI tool, which is listed as a co-author of the paper
options.text: The AI tool, which is listed as a co-author of the paper
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on disclosure rules in scholarly publishing.

options.html: The human authors, for all of the paper's content
options.text: The human authors, for all of the paper's content
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both bodies say the human authors are responsible for everything in the work, including parts an AI tool produced.

options.html: The journal, once it has accepted the authors' disclosure
options.text: The journal, once it has accepted the authors' disclosure
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on disclosure rules in scholarly publishing.

forms.stemHtml: A 2023 study ran seven AI-text detectors on essays written by non-native English speakers. What does its main result show about detectors?

options.html: They catch reworded AI text more reliably than plain AI text
options.text: They catch reworded AI text more reliably than plain AI text
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-text detectors.

options.html: They often label human writing as AI-generated
options.text: They often label human writing as AI-generated
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The detectors wrongly flagged about 61 percent of those human-written essays on average. Errors of that kind are false positives.

options.html: They work equally well for all groups of human writers
options.text: They work equally well for all groups of human writers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-text detectors.

options.html: They fail only on texts that are under a hundred words
options.text: They fail only on texts that are under a hundred words
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-text detectors.

forms.stemHtml: A US federal court sanctioned lawyers over AI-invented cases, and a Canadian tribunal held an airline responsible for its chatbot's false statement. What do the two decisions have in common?

options.html: Each held the user of the AI tool responsible
options.text: Each held the user of the AI tool responsible
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In both, a duty the user already owed stayed with the user. Using a tool didn't transfer it.

options.html: Each held the maker of the AI tool responsible
options.text: Each held the maker of the AI tool responsible
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on accountability and the two decisions.

options.html: Each found that using AI at work is improper
options.text: Each found that using AI at work is improper
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on accountability and the two decisions.

options.html: Each found that nobody could be held responsible
options.text: Each found that nobody could be held responsible
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on accountability and the two decisions.

forms.stemHtml: You turn off the setting that lets a provider use your conversations for training. Going by what providers' own pages describe, which of these may still happen? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The provider keeps your conversations for a period
options.text: The provider keeps your conversations for a period
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Retention is separate from training use and may continue.

options.html: Some conversations are reviewed for safety reasons
options.text: Some conversations are reviewed for safety reasons
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Review is separate from training use and may continue in some circumstances.

options.html: A conversation you rate with a feedback button is used
options.text: A conversation you rate with a feedback button is used
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Providers' pages describe feedback as an exception to the training setting.

options.html: Your new conversations are used for ordinary model training
options.text: Your new conversations are used for ordinary model training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention, human review, and training use.

forms.stemHtml: A teacher pays for her own subscription to an AI assistant. Her school licenses a different assistant for staff. Which arrangement is her own subscription?

options.html: A business account, since she uses it for her work
options.text: A business account, since she uses it for her work
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on consumer, business, and local use.

options.html: An education account, since she is a teacher
options.text: An education account, since she is a teacher
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on consumer, business, and local use.

options.html: A local deployment, since it runs on her laptop
options.text: A local deployment, since it runs on her laptop
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on consumer, business, and local use.

options.html: A consumer account, on the provider's own terms
options.text: A consumer account, on the provider's own terms
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An account an individual opens directly with a provider is a consumer account, whether free or paid.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these should stay out of an AI tool unless a rule you're bound by permits it? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A list of customers with their contact details
options.text: A list of customers with their contact details
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is other people's personal data.

options.html: Your employer's unannounced pricing plan
options.text: Your employer's unannounced pricing plan
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is confidential employer material.

options.html: A paragraph from a published news article
options.text: A paragraph from a published news article
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what to keep out of a prompt.

options.html: A named student's disciplinary notes
options.text: A named student's disciplinary notes
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is a student record.

forms.stemHtml: Under the US Copyright Office's 2025 report, what is the status of an image generated entirely by an AI system from a user's prompt?

options.html: It's protected, and the user holds the copyright
options.text: It's protected, and the user holds the copyright
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on copyright in AI outputs.

options.html: It's protected, and the AI developer holds the copyright
options.text: It's protected, and the AI developer holds the copyright
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on copyright in AI outputs.

options.html: It isn't protected by copyright
options.text: It isn't protected by copyright
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The report says copyright doesn't extend to purely AI-generated material and that prompts alone don't make the user its author.

options.html: It's protected only once the user has published it
options.text: It's protected only once the user has published it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on copyright in AI outputs.

forms.stemHtml: In a field experiment with high school mathematics students, what happened to those who had a standard chatbot during practice and then took an exam without it?

options.html: They scored higher than students who had never had the chatbot
options.text: They scored higher than students who had never had the chatbot
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on learning with and without AI support.

options.html: They scored lower than students who never had it
options.text: They scored lower than students who never had it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Their practice scores rose, and on the later exam without AI they scored 17 percent lower than students who had practiced with no AI.

options.html: They scored the same as students who had never had the chatbot
options.text: They scored the same as students who had never had the chatbot
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on learning with and without AI support.

options.html: They scored lower in practice and higher on the later exam
options.text: They scored lower in practice and higher on the later exam
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on learning with and without AI support.

forms.stemHtml: A study of doctors found that their detection rate in procedures done without AI was lower after their clinics introduced an AI system. The study was observational. What does that limit?

options.html: Whether the detection rates were recorded accurately at all
options.text: Whether the detection rates were recorded accurately at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on skill and critical thinking at work.

options.html: Whether the study can be published in a medical journal
options.text: Whether the study can be published in a medical journal
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on skill and critical thinking at work.

options.html: Whether the doctors can be regarded as experienced
options.text: Whether the doctors can be regarded as experienced
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on skill and critical thinking at work.

options.html: Whether the drop can be credited to the AI system
options.text: Whether the drop can be credited to the AI system
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An observational study doesn't assign people to conditions, so it can't rule out other causes, such as a heavier workload.

forms.stemHtml: Which habits help keep a skill in use while you still get help from AI? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Attempting the task yourself before you ask
options.text: Attempting the task yourself before you ask
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Attempting first means doing your own thinking before the tool's version appears.

options.html: Asking for a hint in place of the answer
options.text: Asking for a hint in place of the answer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A hint points to the next step and leaves the work of taking it to you.

options.html: Restating the result without looking at it
options.text: Restating the result without looking at it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Explaining back checks that you understand the result.

options.html: Asking for the full answer and reading it twice
options.text: Asking for the full answer and reading it twice
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on preserving skill by design.

forms.stemHtml: An author states in her paper that an AI tool drafted the background section. Under the COPE and ICMJE positions, how does that disclosure affect her responsibility for the section?

options.html: It doesn't; she remains fully responsible for it
options.text: It doesn't; she remains fully responsible for it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Disclosure tells readers about the method. It leaves the human authors fully responsible for the content.

options.html: It halves it, since the tool shares the responsibility
options.text: It halves it, since the tool shares the responsibility
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on disclosure rules in scholarly publishing.

options.html: It removes it, since readers have been duly warned
options.text: It removes it, since readers have been duly warned
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on disclosure rules in scholarly publishing.

options.html: It moves it to the editor who approved the paper
options.text: It moves it to the editor who approved the paper
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on disclosure rules in scholarly publishing.

forms.stemHtml: A student who wrote her essay herself, in her second language, is flagged by an AI-text detector. What kind of error is this?

options.html: A false negative, which lets AI-written text pass as human
options.text: A false negative, which lets AI-written text pass as human
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-text detectors.

options.html: A fabricated citation, which points to no real source
options.text: A fabricated citation, which points to no real source
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-text detectors.

options.html: A negligent misrepresentation by the student herself
options.text: A negligent misrepresentation by the student herself
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-text detectors.

options.html: A false positive, which labels human writing as AI
options.text: A false positive, which labels human writing as AI
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A false positive is a detector's labeling of human writing as AI-generated. A 2023 study found such errors were common for non-native English writers.

forms.stemHtml: An airline argued before a tribunal that its website chatbot was a separate legal entity responsible for its own actions. How did the tribunal respond?

options.html: It agreed, and dismissed the customer's claim against the airline
options.text: It agreed, and dismissed the customer's claim against the airline
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on accountability and the two decisions.

options.html: It agreed, and ordered the chatbot's developer to pay instead
options.text: It agreed, and ordered the chatbot's developer to pay instead
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on accountability and the two decisions.

options.html: It declined to rule, since the law on chatbots is unsettled
options.text: It declined to rule, since the law on chatbots is unsettled
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on accountability and the two decisions.

options.html: It rejected the argument and held the airline responsible
options.text: It rejected the argument and held the airline responsible
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The tribunal held the airline responsible for all the information on its website, whether it came from a static page or a chatbot.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these are separate things a provider can do with your conversations, each needing its own answer? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Keeping them on its systems for a period
options.text: Keeping them on its systems for a period
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is data retention.

options.html: Having people read some of them
options.text: Having people read some of them
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is human review.

options.html: Using them to improve its models
options.text: Using them to improve its models
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is training use.

options.html: Showing them to other users of the tool
options.text: Showing them to other users of the tool
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention, human review, and training use.

forms.stemHtml: What makes an account a consumer account, as opposed to one under enterprise terms?

options.html: An individual opened it directly with the provider
options.text: An individual opened it directly with the provider
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A consumer account is opened by an individual, free or paid. Enterprise terms come from a contract between the provider and an organization.

options.html: The account is free, with no monthly payment required
options.text: The account is free, with no monthly payment required
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on consumer, business, and local use.

options.html: The account is used at home and not in an office building
options.text: The account is used at home and not in an office building
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on consumer, business, and local use.

options.html: The account runs a smaller model than business accounts do
options.text: The account runs a smaller model than business accounts do
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on consumer, business, and local use.

forms.stemHtml: A school counselor is deciding what she can paste into an AI tool that her school hasn't approved. Which of these should she keep out? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: A student's accommodation plan
options.text: A student's accommodation plan
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is a student record, and it contains health-related information.

options.html: Her own draft of a general study-skills handout
options.text: Her own draft of a general study-skills handout
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what to keep out of a prompt.

options.html: A parent's email about a family's finances
options.text: A parent's email about a family's finances
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is another person's personal and financial information.

options.html: A colleague's notes on a named student
options.text: A colleague's notes on a named student
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is a record about an identifiable student.

forms.stemHtml: A shop owner types one sentence into an AI tool and uses the slogan it returns, unchanged. Under the US Copyright Office's position, can she stop a competitor from copying it?

options.html: Yes, since she wrote the prompt that produced the slogan
options.text: Yes, since she wrote the prompt that produced the slogan
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on copyright in AI outputs.

options.html: Yes, since she was the first to use the slogan in public
options.text: Yes, since she was the first to use the slogan in public
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on copyright in AI outputs.

options.html: Yes, since she paid for the AI tool that produced it
options.text: Yes, since she paid for the AI tool that produced it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on copyright in AI outputs.

options.html: Perhaps not, since copyright may not protect it
options.text: Perhaps not, since copyright may not protect it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Purely AI-generated material isn't protected by copyright in the United States, and a prompt alone doesn't make the user its author.

forms.stemHtml: A trainee uses a chatbot to get the answer to every practice exercise and scores very well on them. Going by the controlled studies of students, what is the likely result when she is tested without the chatbot?

options.html: She does better than trainees who practiced without AI
options.text: She does better than trainees who practiced without AI
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on learning with and without AI support.

options.html: She does about as well as she did on the practice exercises
options.text: She does about as well as she did on the practice exercises
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on learning with and without AI support.

options.html: She does well, because high practice scores predict test scores
options.text: She does well, because high practice scores predict test scores
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on learning with and without AI support.

options.html: She does worse than trainees who practiced without AI
options.text: She does worse than trainees who practiced without AI
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! In the mathematics study, answers on demand raised practice performance and lowered unassisted performance.

forms.stemHtml: A survey finds that workers who trust AI more report thinking less critically. Why can't this show that trusting AI causes less critical thinking?

options.html: A survey shows that two things go together, not why
options.text: A survey shows that two things go together, not why
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The finding is a correlation based on self-report. People may also trust AI most on tasks that needed little thought.

options.html: A survey of several hundred people is always too small
options.text: A survey of several hundred people is always too small
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on skill and critical thinking at work.

options.html: A survey can be answered only by people who use AI daily
options.text: A survey can be answered only by people who use AI daily
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on skill and critical thinking at work.

options.html: A survey has to be repeated before it can be reported
options.text: A survey has to be repeated before it can be reported
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on skill and critical thinking at work.

forms.stemHtml: A new teacher wants to keep developing her skill at writing feedback on student essays while using an AI assistant. Using invented sample essays, which approaches would exercise the skill? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Writing her own comments, then asking what she missed
options.text: Writing her own comments, then asking what she missed
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is attempting first and then asking for critique.

options.html: Having the assistant write the comments and sending them on
options.text: Having the assistant write the comments and sending them on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on preserving skill by design.

options.html: Writing feedback on one essay a week with no AI
options.text: Writing feedback on one essay a week with no AI
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is unaided practice on a schedule.

options.html: Explaining aloud why each comment she kept is right
options.text: Explaining aloud why each comment she kept is right
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is explaining back, which checks her understanding.

forms.stemHtml: Why do COPE and the ICMJE say that an AI tool can't be listed as an author?

options.html: Because its text is less accurate than a person's writing
options.text: Because its text is less accurate than a person's writing
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on disclosure rules in scholarly publishing.

options.html: Because readers would trust the paper less if it were
options.text: Because readers would trust the paper less if it were
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on disclosure rules in scholarly publishing.

options.html: Because the tool's developer would then own the paper
options.text: Because the tool's developer would then own the paper
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on disclosure rules in scholarly publishing.

options.html: Because it can't take responsibility for the work
options.text: Because it can't take responsibility for the work
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Authorship carries responsibility for the work, and both bodies say an AI tool can't take it. The human authors do.

forms.stemHtml: A manager receives a detector report saying an employee's memo is "likely AI-generated." Going by the published evidence on detectors, how should the report be treated?

options.html: As proof that the employee used an AI tool to write it
options.text: As proof that the employee used an AI tool to write it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-text detectors.

options.html: As proof that the employee broke the company's policy
options.text: As proof that the employee broke the company's policy
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-text detectors.

options.html: As a reason to talk with the employee, and not as proof
options.text: As a reason to talk with the employee, and not as proof
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Detectors have wrongly flagged human writing at high rates, so a flag can't establish that someone used AI.

options.html: As reliable, so long as the memo is longer than one page
options.text: As reliable, so long as the memo is longer than one page
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI-text detectors.

forms.stemHtml: A consultant sends a client a report containing a wrong figure that an AI assistant supplied. Following the reasoning of the two decisions on AI errors, who answers for the figure?

options.html: The assistant's developer, since its product made the error
options.text: The assistant's developer, since its product made the error
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on accountability and the two decisions.

options.html: The client, who should have checked the report's figures
options.text: The client, who should have checked the report's figures
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on accountability and the two decisions.

options.html: The consultant, whose name is on the report
options.text: The consultant, whose name is on the report
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Using a tool doesn't transfer a duty of care. The consultant's name on the report is an assurance of its contents.

options.html: Nobody, since the error came from an automated tool
options.text: Nobody, since the error came from an automated tool
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on accountability and the two decisions.

forms.stemHtml: A colleague says, "I opted out of training, so my chats are private now." Which facts would you point to in reply? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Opting out doesn't delete conversations already stored
options.text: Opting out doesn't delete conversations already stored
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A training setting leaves retention as it was.

options.html: Opting out makes the provider erase its copies at once
options.text: Opting out makes the provider erase its copies at once
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on retention, human review, and training use.

options.html: Conversations flagged for safety may still be examined
options.text: Conversations flagged for safety may still be examined
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Review can continue whatever the training setting says.

options.html: Providers' terms differ, so the current page must be read
options.text: Providers' terms differ, so the current page must be read
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each provider publishes its own practices, and the pages change.

forms.stemHtml: An accountant uses his personal paid AI account to summarize a client's files, reasoning that it's a work task. What is wrong with that reasoning?

options.html: Paid personal accounts can't summarize long documents
options.text: Paid personal accounts can't summarize long documents
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on consumer, business, and local use.

options.html: A personal account isn't a work tool under a contract
options.text: A personal account isn't a work tool under a contract
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The kind of task doesn't change the arrangement. A personal account is a consumer account, on terms his firm and client never agreed to.

options.html: Personal accounts always train on every conversation
options.text: Personal accounts always train on every conversation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on consumer, business, and local use.

options.html: A work task can only be done on a locally run model
options.text: A work task can only be done on a locally run model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on consumer, business, and local use.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these kinds of information belong to someone other than you, so that a rule is likely to govern whether they go into an AI tool? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Notes you wrote on a book you read
options.text: Notes you wrote on a book you read
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on what to keep out of a prompt.

options.html: A coworker's medical leave details
options.text: A coworker's medical leave details
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Health information about another person is among the most protected kinds.

options.html: A client's draft contract
options.text: A client's draft contract
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is confidential client material.

options.html: Salary data for your team
options.text: Salary data for your team
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is financial information about identifiable people.

forms.stemHtml: Why does the US Copyright Office say a prompt alone doesn't make the user the author of an AI system's output?

options.html: A prompt doesn't give enough human control
options.text: A prompt doesn't give enough human control
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The Office treats a prompt as an instruction that conveys an idea. The system decides how to express it, and copyright protects human expression.

options.html: A prompt is too short to count as writing
options.text: A prompt is too short to count as writing
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on copyright in AI outputs.

options.html: A prompt belongs to the AI tool's developer
options.text: A prompt belongs to the AI tool's developer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on copyright in AI outputs.

options.html: A prompt must first be registered with the Office
options.text: A prompt must first be registered with the Office
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on copyright in AI outputs.

forms.stemHtml: In the high school mathematics study, a tutor version of the chatbot largely avoided the harm to later exam scores. How did it differ from the standard chatbot?

options.html: It was built on a newer and more capable AI model
options.text: It was built on a newer and more capable AI model
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on learning with and without AI support.

options.html: It was available to students for many more sessions
options.text: It was available to students for many more sessions
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on learning with and without AI support.

options.html: It gave hints and held back the answer
options.text: It gave hints and held back the answer
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The tutor version was instructed to give hints without giving away the answer, which kept students doing the work.

options.html: It was used only by the strongest students in each class
options.text: It was used only by the strongest students in each class
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on learning with and without AI support.

forms.stemHtml: A news story says a brain-recording study proves that chatbots damage thinking. The study is a preprint with 54 participants, and other researchers have disputed its methods. How strong is this as evidence of lasting harm?

options.html: Strong, since brain recordings are objective measurements
options.text: Strong, since brain recordings are objective measurements
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on skill and critical thinking at work.

options.html: Strong, since it was reported widely in the news
options.text: Strong, since it was reported widely in the news
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on skill and critical thinking at work.

options.html: Weak, since it's small, unreviewed, and disputed
options.text: Weak, since it's small, unreviewed, and disputed
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A preprint hasn't been reviewed by independent experts, and a difference in brain activity during a task isn't the same as lasting harm.

options.html: Worthless, since preprints never contain real findings
options.text: Worthless, since preprints never contain real findings
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on skill and critical thinking at work.

forms.stemHtml: An analyst has decided she needs to keep her skill at interpreting charts. Which changes to how she uses an AI assistant fit that goal? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Asking the assistant to interpret each chart before she looks
options.text: Asking the assistant to interpret each chart before she looks
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on preserving skill by design.

options.html: Writing her own interpretation before she asks
options.text: Writing her own interpretation before she asks
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is attempting first.

options.html: Asking the assistant to critique her interpretation
options.text: Asking the assistant to critique her interpretation
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Critique keeps her doing the interpreting while still getting help.

options.html: Interpreting some charts each month with no AI
options.text: Interpreting some charts each month with no AI
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! This is unaided practice, which also shows her whether the skill is still there.

title: Responsible Use
